keyFindings.description: Architect-required (INFRA-14's finding): the stream_recreated check (703) compares JetStream's `created` time, which differs between a clustered stream's leader and followers and changes at a leader election, so an election or a read from another replica resets every session's cursors and tells each that messages may be missing. Stream identity must come from an id kept in the stream config's metadata, preserved by the listener's reconcile, restores and elections, and an upgrade from stream_created state must not reset anyone.

The gap notice is now lost when the session ends while the gap write is in flight: flush checks alive() only before host.write (463), so the lifted cursor is persisted, then `if (!alive()) return` (743) skips the notice, and every restore finds no gap. Real in claude-envoy (async atomic file write; shutdown on plugin reload, /clear); both agents reproduced it (notices [] before and after the restart; round 5's order told it once). Persist the untold notice with the lift (e.g. a gap_untold flag in ReplayState written by the same flush, raised and cleared by the next sweep or restore), and apply the same rule to the stream-identity notice.
The no-auth NATS user sentence assumes the peers that reach port 9020 also reach the NATS client port; tailnet rules are per port. Say 'peers the access rules also let reach NATS'.
